title: Blood Orange Chocolate Tart with Jelly Top
changes_from_base: A cocoa pastry case, an unbaked ganache instead of the baked chocolate custard, and a blood orange jelly layer set with beef gelatine.
summary: A cocoa pastry case filled with blood orange ganache and topped with a glossy ruby blood orange jelly.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: check the label for milk and soya

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cocoa dough
steps.text: whisk the yolk, cream and vanilla. Pulse the flour, cocoa, icing sugar and salt, scatter the butter over and pulse about 15 times, then add the yolk mix with the motor running until it gathers. Wrap and chill 1 h.

steps.title: Shape the shell
steps.text: roll to a 28 cm round, line the tin, trim the top and freeze 30 min. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake blind
steps.text: fill with paper and beans and bake on the tray about 30 min, then 5 min uncovered, until dry and fragrant. Cool fully, about 30 min.

steps.title: Ganache
steps.text: bring the cream, zest and salt to a simmer, take off the heat, add the chocolate and cover for 5 min. Whisk smooth, then whisk in the butter and vanilla. Spread in the case and chill at least 2 h.

steps.title: Jelly
steps.text: sprinkle the gelatine over 60 ml of the juice and leave 5 min. Warm the remaining juice with the zest, sugar and salt for about 3 min, just until the sugar dissolves. Whisk in the soaked gelatine off the heat, sieve, and cool 15 min. Pour only when it is cool, or it will melt the ganache.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: trickle the cool jelly gently over the set ganache and chill about 3 h, until firm.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: cut the peel and pith from the last orange, slice out the segments and arrange them in a small pinwheel in the centre just before slicing. Add the segments at the last minute so their juice does not run.

tips: Let the jelly cool for 15 minutes before pouring, or it will melt the ganache.
Check that the gelatine packet clearly says beef before you buy it.
Ordinary oranges work too, but the jelly will be paler.
Chill the tart on a level shelf so the jelly sets evenly.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 1 day after adding the jelly. Do not freeze.
